name: Lumbar Spondylosis / Degenerative Disc-Facet Disease
definition: Degenerative change involving lumbar discs, vertebral endplates, osteophytes and facet joints. Imaging abnormalities are common in asymptomatic adults and require clinical correlation.

typical: May coexist with radiculopathy or stenosis

redFlags.item: New bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle sensory loss or progressive weakness
Fever/systemic illness, major trauma, cancer-related red flags or suspected fracture

investigations.principle: Do not image routine uncomplicated low-back pain solely to document degeneration.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neurological deficit, red flags or persistent symptoms would change management.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs may show disc-height loss, osteophytes, alignment and facet degeneration.

green: Education and continuation of appropriate activity
amber: Medication, injection or procedural decisions require individualized risk review; imaging findings alone must not determine treatment.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Possible Kati-shoola/Kati-graha or Vata-dominant symptom overlap may be documented as correlation only.

patientEducation.summary: Degenerative change involving lumbar discs, vertebral endplates, osteophytes and facet joints. Imaging abnormalities are common in asymptomatic adults and require clinical correlation.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for new/progressive major weakness, gait deterioration, bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle sensory loss, fever/systemic illness with severe spinal/joint pain, major trauma, or other listed red flags.
